name: Zurich
limitations: All 31 subpillars are reviewed, not all are measured. Scores require the stated assumptions; unknown evidence remains unknown. This is neither a global ranking nor an exclusion bound. Rejecting a necessary assumption requires reassessment, not automatic retention of its score.

dimensions.rationale: Implemented monitoring and cooling actions support protection, while heat exposure and protection against other hazards remain incompletely measured.
dimensions.assumption: Implemented measures usually work and unreviewed places do not already face broader unmitigated failure. Dynamic descriptions do not establish delivery dates or whole-FUA coverage.

dimensions.rationale: Cantonal risk management supports mitigation while regional conflict and strategic risks persist; no matched historical event does not establish low current local violence.
dimensions.assumption: Ordinary life is not broadly and persistently blocked. Risk registers and programme progress are neither local event rates nor failure probabilities.

dimensions.rationale: Resident survey evidence and implemented risk management support partial execution and social connection; group reach and actual crisis recovery remain incomplete.
dimensions.assumption: Observed execution persists and supports usual major-service operation; municipal perceptions and cantonal measures are not whole-FUA outcomes.

dimensions.rationale: Actual water delivery during the 2026 heat and drought and national stock reconciliation support supply; common water, power and logistics dependencies remain.
dimensions.assumption: Essential resources are usually available and affordable at median income. Municipal service areas and national inventories do not measure the whole FUA or last-mile crisis delivery.

dimensions.rationale: Basic insurance eligibility and actual specialist delivery support care pathways; costs, historical cardiac-surgery failures and current-quality verification remain material constraints.
dimensions.assumption: Necessary care is usually obtainable, clinically adequate and affordable under usual coverage. Historical failures are not current mortality rates; remediation claims are not independently recalculated outcomes.

dimensions.rationale: Local human research is verified, but the reviewed pathway has a gap between primary clinical outcomes and current resident adoption. Clock changes do not establish clinical benefit; a later fall analysis retains possible benefit.
dimensions.assumption: The reviewed pathway is sufficiently representative to support limited translation capability. Rejecting this assumption leaves LON unresolved, rather than assuming other pathways do not exist or retaining 40.

dimensions.rationale: Concrete research, defined commercialisation organisations and fixed/mobile samples support capability; sustained whole-FUA output, industry density and resident diffusion remain incomplete.
dimensions.assumption: Observed capability persists and technology is usually usable. Institutional prominence and recognition counts do not fill missing adoption or whole-population coverage measurements.

dimensions.rationale: Operating rail and aviation, conditional mobility rights and pension payment pathways support exit channels; account conditions and the future-dated mobile backup mandate constrain high-tier inference.
dimensions.assumption: Median-income residents usually have usable travel and relocation funds, accounts and communications. Existing services usually persist to the cutoff; summer timetables are not current crisis capacity.
